name: Space Exploration Encounter
description: p.88. Roll 1D when jumping to an unmapped parsec hex on a subsector map. Sector Density DMs: Rift or assumed empty sectors -2DM; Sparse sectors -1DM; Typical density sectors +0DM; Densely populated sectors +1DM.

results.text: Uninhabitated star system (0 or less)
Empty (1-3)
Inhabitated system encounter (4+). Generate the star system and the main world.

name: Primary Star Table
description: p.88. Roll 2D and add the Sector Density DM (Rift or assumed empty -2DM; Sparse -1DM; Typical +0DM; Densely populated +1DM). Mass (M): 1M equals the mass of Earth's Sun. Radius (R): 1 radius equals the radius of Earth's Sun. 1 AU equals 1.5 million kilometres. The book lists no result for 9; this table gives 9 to the G row (6-9).

name: Other Stellar Objects
description: p.89. For every generated planet, roll 2D. Moons: to determine the size of each moon, roll a D3-1 per moon on Step 1 of the World generator.

results.text: Unique Celestial Observation: Use the Unique Celestial Observation table to determine what type is found within this star system.
Barren: Rock ball, devoid of atmosphere. May have industrial facilities or small colonies. Barren planets will have D3 moons.
Gas Giant: Gas giants will have 1D moons around them. These moons may function as bases for pirates, corporations, or other groups who use the gas giant as a source of revenue or ambushes.

Structure: This represents notable or important man- or sophont-made structures. Roll 1D
1) Belter base
2) Communication or remote research station
3) Remote starbase port station
4) Scrap or salvage base
5) Colony cluster: 1D colonies
6) Abandoned structure with a 50% chance of being occupied by squatters, pirates, or other spacers. Roll D3 on this list to determine the type of abandoned structure.
Secondary World: An inhabited world, a minor planet to the main world in the star system.

name: Structure Type (Other Stellar Objects)
description: p.89. Roll 1D when the Other Stellar Objects table gives a Structure (9-11). For an abandoned structure, roll D3 on this list to determine the type of abandoned structure.

name: Unique Celestial Observation Table
description: p.89. Roll 2D to determine the unique observation in the star system.

results.text: Anomaly: A strange artificial celestial body exists within the system either as a stellar object/event or as a planetside anomaly. See the Anomalies Table to determine what type is observed.

Shattered World: A planet or planetoid that has been hit by another celestial body, shattering it in many large pieces. This world still has its normal orbit but is a hazard because of the debris that is slingshot from its fractured form. Pilot checks incur -1DM while moving through this system.

Cluster: A massive cloud of asteroids or planetoids made of minerals and ice clutter a large portion of the system, making travel difficult, providing -2DM to pilot checks and -1DM to Astrogation. Roll D3 to determine the cluster's shape: 1) Torus 2) spherical 3) asymmetrical
Secondary Star: There is a secondary star that is twice as weak as the primary star. Jumping is -2DM.

Black Hole: There is a black hole that is the primary gravitational body, but the sun and planets exist outside of the Schwartzchild radius of the black hole, allowing for the planets and star to not be pulled in. Jumping in and out of this system is -3DM.
